Test Scenario Name: View Flashcards in an owned Deck
Test scenarios' Precondition overall: The application is available. Learner A is signed in with an Active account. Test Decks are ready.
Test Condition Name: An owned Deck shows its Flashcards or the empty message
Test Case Summary: Show all Flashcards in an owned Deck
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns a non-empty Deck with a known set of Flashcards.
Steps: 1. Sign in as Learner A. 2. Set TD-DOC-DECK-001 to the populated state, open Library, and open that Deck. 3. Compare the Deck name, card count, and card content with TD-DOC-DECK-001. 4. Reload the page.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The correct Deck name and card count are shown. Each current Flashcard shows its Term, Meaning, and Example sentence, and no card from another Deck appears. The same data remains after reload.

Test Case Summary: Show the empty message for an owned Deck
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns an empty Deck.
Steps: 1. Sign in as Learner A. 2. Set TD-DOC-DECK-001 to the empty state and open that Deck. 3. Observe the content area and available creation actions.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The page shows "This Deck has no Flashcards yet" without an error. Create manually and Create with AI remain available, and Export is disabled.

Test Condition Name: A missing Deck or another Learner's Deck does not show content
Test Case Summary: Show Deck unavailable after it was deleted
Test Preconditions: Learner A has a saved URL for a Deck that has since been deleted.
Steps: 1. Sign in as Learner A. 2. Open the saved URL for the deleted Deck. 3. Select Try again if the option is shown.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] A Deck unavailable or Unable to load Deck message is shown. No Flashcard content or edit control appears.

Test Case Summary: Block direct URL access to another Learner's Deck
Test Preconditions: Learner B owns a non-empty Deck; Learner A knows its Deck URL.
Steps: 1. Sign in as Learner A, who does not own the target Deck. 2. Open Learner B's Deck URL from TD-DOC-DECK-003. 3. Observe the page and reload it.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Access denied or Deck unavailable is shown. Learner B's Deck name, count, Flashcards, and edit controls are not shown.

Test Case Summary: Open a Deck URL with a Deck ID that does not exist
Steps: 1. In the browser, open a Deck Flashcard-list URL with a valid-format Deck ID that does not exist. 2. Observe the page.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] A Not Found or Deck unavailable message is shown. No Deck name, Flashcard content, or edit control is displayed.
Execution Notes: Perspective: Negative | Technique: Error Guessing / Invalid Resource

Test scenarios' Precondition overall: The application is available. Learner A is signed in with an Active account and owns the target Decks.
Test Condition Name: Valid manual content is saved with the initial learning state
Test Case Summary: Save manual Japanese content with the initial learning state
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns a target Deck with no duplicate normalized Terms. The TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values are recorded.
Steps: 1. Record the TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values. 2. For each Japanese text test case in TD-DOC-FC-001, open Create manually in the owned Deck. 3. Enter the test Term, Meaning, and Example sentence. 4. Select Create Flashcard and reload the Deck. 5. Compare the related module values with the starting values.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each non-empty Japanese text set is saved and shown exactly as entered after leading and trailing spaces are removed. The manual form does not check vocabulary meaning or require a reading format. 2. [DB] One Flashcard row is created for each test case with the correct owner and Deck, review_level=0, next_review=NULL, and last_recall_rating=NULL. TD-DOC-XMOD-001 values do not change.

Test Case Summary: Save manual Chinese content with the initial learning state
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns a target Deck with no duplicate normalized Terms. The TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values are recorded.
Steps: 1. Record the TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values. 2. For each Chinese text test case in TD-DOC-FC-002, open Create manually in the owned Deck. 3. Enter the test Term, Meaning, and Example sentence. 4. Select Create Flashcard and reload the Deck. 5. Compare the related module values with the starting values.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each non-empty Chinese text set is saved and shown exactly as entered after leading and trailing spaces are removed. The manual form does not check vocabulary meaning or require Pinyin or another reading format. 2. [DB] One Flashcard row is created for each test case with the correct owner and Deck, review_level=0, next_review=NULL, and last_recall_rating=NULL. TD-DOC-XMOD-001 values do not change.

Test Case Summary: Accept maximum field lengths when creating a Flashcard
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns an empty target Deck.
Steps: 1. Open Create manually in the target Deck from TD-DOC-DECK-001. 2. Execute the exact-maximum Term, Meaning, and Example sentence test cases in TD-DOC-FC-003 one at a time while keeping the other fields valid. 3. Submit each test case and reload the saved card. 4. Reset before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Values at Term=500, Meaning=1000, and Example sentence=500 characters are accepted in their separate test cases. 2. [DB] One row per test case is inserted with the exact allowed lengths and no truncation.

Test Case Summary: Remove leading and trailing spaces when creating a Flashcard
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns an empty target Deck.
Steps: 1. Open Create manually in the target Deck. 2. For each trim test case in TD-DOC-FC-003, add leading and trailing spaces to one field and keep the other fields valid. 3. Create and reopen the Flashcard. 4. Reset before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The Flashcard is created and displayed without the added leading and trailing spaces. 2. [DB] The saved field has no leading or trailing spaces. Text inside the value is unchanged, and no unrelated row changes.

Test Case Summary: Keep line breaks when creating a Flashcard
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns an empty target Deck.
Steps: 1. Open Create manually in the target Deck from TD-DOC-DECK-001. 2. Enter the multiline Term, Meaning, and Example sentence data from TD-DOC-FC-003. 3. Submit the Flashcard. 4. Inspect the list/card view, reopen the editor, and reload the Deck.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The Flashcard is created and all test line breaks remain visible after reopen and reload. 2. [DB] The inserted row preserves newline characters in all applicable fields and has the initial SRS state.

Test Case Summary: Recreate a deleted Term from another open session
Test Preconditions: Two authenticated sessions for Learner A have opened the same owned Deck containing the target Flashcard.
Steps: 1. Open the same Deck in two Learner A sessions. 2. In Session 2, open Create manually and keep the page/form open. 3. In Session 1, delete the target Flashcard. 4. Without reloading Session 2, enter the deleted Term with new valid Meaning and Example sentence values and submit. 5. Reload both sessions.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Session 2 creates the Flashcard without a false duplicate error; after reload exactly one card with the target Term and new content is shown. 2. [DB] The original row remains deleted and exactly one new row exists with a new ID, the same normalized Term, and initial SRS values.
Execution Notes: Perspective: Positive/Concurrency/Edge | Technique: State Transition/Error Guessing

Test Condition Name: Invalid or duplicate manual content is not saved
Test Case Summary: Reject blank required fields when creating a Flashcard
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns a target Deck; create form is available.
Steps: 1. Open Create manually in the target Deck from TD-DOC-DECK-001. 2. Execute the blank/whitespace Term, Meaning, and Example sentence test cases in TD-DOC-FC-004 one at a time while keeping the other fields valid. 3. Attempt Create Flashcard. 4. Reset before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each test case is blocked with a required-field message for the affected field. No success message or new card appears. 2. [DB] No Flashcard row is created and the Deck remains unchanged.

Test Case Summary: Reject fields over the maximum length when creating a Flashcard
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns a target Deck; create form is available.
Steps: 1. Open Create manually in the target Deck from TD-DOC-DECK-001. 2. Execute Term=501, Meaning=1001, and Example sentence=501 character test cases in TD-DOC-FC-004 one at a time while keeping the other fields valid. 3. Attempt Create Flashcard. 4. Reset before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each test case is blocked with a length message for the affected field. No success message or new card appears. 2. [DB] No Flashcard row is created and the Deck remains unchanged.

Test Case Summary: Reject duplicate Terms in the same Deck
Test Preconditions: Target Deck already contains a saved card.
Steps: 1. Set TD-DOC-DECK-001 to the populated starting state. 2. For each separate duplicate test case in TD-DOC-FC-005, select Create manually. 3. Enter the duplicate Term variant with otherwise valid content and submit. 4. Reset before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each Term that matches an existing Term after normalization is rejected with a duplicate message. The card count and original card do not change. 2. [DB] No new Flashcard row is created. The original row is unchanged, and the same Deck does not contain two rows with the same term_normalized value.

Test Case Summary: Allow only one concurrent create for the same Term
Test Preconditions: Two authenticated browser sessions for Learner A can access the same Deck.
Steps: 1. Open Create Flashcard for the same Deck in two browser sessions. 2. Enter valid content in both forms, using Terms that become equal after normalization. 3. Submit both forms as closely together as possible. 4. Reload the Deck in both sessions.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Exactly one submission succeeds. The other shows a duplicate message. After reload, only one matching card is shown. 2. [DB] Only one new Flashcard row exists for the normalized Term. No partial or duplicate row exists.

Test Condition Name: Create fails if the Deck or parent Folder no longer exists
Test Case Summary: Reject create if the Deck is deleted before submit
Test Preconditions: Two signed-in Learner A sessions can access the same owned Deck; Session 2 has its Create Flashcard form open.
Steps: 1. Open the same owned Deck in two Learner A sessions. 2. In Session 2, open Create manually and enter valid TD-DOC-FC-001 content without submitting. 3. In Session 1, delete the target Deck and complete confirmation if required. 4. Without reloading Session 2, submit the form. 5. Reload Library in both sessions.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Session 2 receives a Deck unavailable/Not Found response; no success toast or new Flashcard appears and the Deck remains absent. 2. [DB] The target 'decks' row remains deleted, no rows are inserted by the stale create request, and no orphan Flashcard exists.
Execution Notes: Perspective: Negative/Concurrency/Integrity | Technique: State Transition/Error Guessing

Test Case Summary: Reject create if the parent Folder is deleted before submit
Test Preconditions: Two signed-in Learner A sessions can access the same owned Folder and child Deck; Session 2 has the child Deck create form open.
Steps: 1. Open the same child Deck in two Learner A sessions. 2. In Session 2, open Create manually and enter valid TD-DOC-FC-001 content without submitting. 3. In Session 1, delete the parent Folder and confirm cascade deletion. 4. Without reloading Session 2, submit the form. 5. Reload Library in both sessions.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Session 2 receives a Deck unavailable/Not Found response; no success toast appears and the deleted Folder/Deck remain absent. 2. [DB] The parent Folder and target Deck remain deleted, no rows are inserted by the stale request, no resource is recreated, and no orphan Flashcard exists.
Execution Notes: Perspective: Negative/Concurrency/Cascade Integrity | Technique: State Transition/Error Guessing

Test scenarios' Precondition overall: Learner A is signed in with an Active account and owns editable Flashcards.
Test Condition Name: A valid edit changes content only
Test Case Summary: Edit content without changing the Deck or SRS state
Test Preconditions: The owned Flashcard's Deck, content, and SRS values are recorded. TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values are recorded.
Steps: 1. Record the TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting state. 2. Open the owned Flashcard and change the test content fields. 3. Select Save changes. 4. Reopen and reload the card. 5. Compare Dashboard/notification state with the starting state.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] A success message appears and the edited values remain after reload. No move-to-Deck control is shown. 2. [DB] Only the submitted content and updated_at change. Owner, Deck, SRS, notification, study, and activity values do not change.

Test Case Summary: Accept maximum field lengths when editing a Flashcard
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns editable Japanese and Chinese cards.
Steps: 1. For each exact-maximum test case in TD-DOC-FC-003, open the editable card from TD-DOC-FC-006. 2. Set Term=500, Meaning=1000, or Example sentence=500 characters while keeping the other fields valid. 3. Save changes and reopen the card. 4. Reset before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Every exact-maximum test case saves successfully without truncation. 2. [DB] The target row contains the exact allowed value while owner, Deck association, and SRS columns remain unchanged.

Test Case Summary: Keep line breaks when editing a Flashcard
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns editable Japanese and Chinese cards.
Steps: 1. Open the editable Flashcard from TD-DOC-FC-006. 2. Apply the multiline content data from TD-DOC-FC-003. 3. Save changes. 4. Reopen the editor and reload the Deck.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The edited multiline content remains visible with the test line breaks after reopen and reload. 2. [DB] Newline characters are preserved and Deck/SRS columns remain unchanged.

Test Condition Name: An invalid or duplicate edit keeps saved data unchanged
Test Case Summary: Reject blank fields when editing and keep the old data
Test Preconditions: The current content, updated_at value, Deck, and SRS state of the owned Flashcard are recorded.
Steps: 1. For each blank/whitespace test case in TD-DOC-FC-004, open the saved card from TD-DOC-FC-006. 2. Clear one required field while keeping the others valid. 3. Attempt Save changes. 4. Reload and compare with the starting state; reset before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each save is blocked with a required-field message, and the previous content remains after reload. 2. [DB] The Flashcard row is not updated. Its content, updated_at value, Deck, and SRS state do not change.

Test Case Summary: Reject over-limit fields when editing and keep the old data
Test Preconditions: The current content, updated_at value, Deck, and SRS state of the owned Flashcard are recorded.
Steps: 1. For each one-over-limit test case in TD-DOC-FC-004, open the saved card from TD-DOC-FC-006. 2. Set Term=501, Meaning=1001, or Example sentence=501 characters while keeping the others valid. 3. Attempt Save changes. 4. Reload and compare with the starting state; reset before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each save is blocked with a length message, and the previous content remains after reload. 2. [DB] The Flashcard row is not updated. Its content, updated_at value, Deck, and SRS state do not change.

Test Case Summary: Reject a duplicate Term when editing
Test Preconditions: The Deck contains at least two Flashcards with different normalized Terms.
Steps: 1. Open the target card from TD-DOC-FC-006. 2. For each case, whitespace, and Unicode duplicate test case in TD-DOC-FC-005, change Term to the conflicting value. 3. Select Save changes. 4. Reload and compare both cards; reset before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each conflict is rejected with a duplicate response and both original cards retain their prior Terms. 2. [DB] No rows are updated and the unique Deck/normalized-Term boundary remains enforced.

Test Condition Name: A missing Flashcard or another Learner's Flashcard cannot be edited
Test Case Summary: Reject edit if the Flashcard is deleted before save
Test Preconditions: Two Learner A sessions can access the same owned Flashcard. Session 2 has the editor open.
Steps: 1. Open the same Flashcard in two Learner A sessions. 2. In Session 2, edit valid content without saving. 3. In Session 1, delete the Flashcard. 4. Without reloading Session 2, select Save changes. 5. Reload both sessions.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Session 2 receives an unavailable/Not Found response; no edit success toast appears and the card remains absent. 2. [DB] The deleted row is not recreated or updated and no replacement/partial row exists.

Test scenarios' Precondition overall: Learner A is signed in with an Active account and owns Flashcards that can be deleted.
Test Condition Name: Delete removes the Flashcard immediately
Test Case Summary: Delete an owned Flashcard without confirmation
Test Preconditions: The owned Deck contains the target Flashcard. Its SRS state and TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values are recorded.
Steps: 1. Record the target card, its SRS state, and TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values. 2. Open the owned Deck and select Delete Flashcard. 3. Check whether a confirmation dialog appears. 4. Reload the Deck and compare the recorded values.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] No confirmation is required; a success toast appears, count decreases by one, and the card remains absent after reload. 2. [DB] The target row and SRS state are deleted; other cards and TD-DOC-XMOD-001 values remain unchanged.

Test Case Summary: Remove a deleted Flashcard from all related views
Test Preconditions: The target card is visible before deletion in LEARN, DASH, the public shared view, and an export.
Steps: 1. Record where the target card appears in LEARN, DASH, the public shared view, and the exported workbook. 2. Delete the card from the Deck. 3. Reload LEARN, DASH, and the public shared view, then export the Deck again.
Expected Result: 1. [UI/File] The deleted card no longer appears in LEARN, DASH, the refreshed public view, or the new workbook. 2. [DB] The target Flashcard row no longer exists and related queries cannot return it. Other cards, share settings, profile activity, and notifications do not change.

Test Case Summary: Delete a Flashcard from a stale page after another session edits it
Test Preconditions: Two Learner A sessions have the same owned Flashcard open. Its content and SRS state are recorded.
Steps: 1. Open the same Flashcard in Session A and Session B. 2. Keep Session B open without reloading. 3. In Session A, edit valid content and save it. 4. Without reloading Session B, delete that Flashcard. 5. Reload both sessions and open the Deck.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Session B deletes the Flashcard without confirmation. After reload, the card is missing in both sessions and the Deck count is lower by one. 2. [DB] The Flashcard row, including the latest content saved by Session A and its SRS state, is deleted. Other Flashcards do not change.

Test Condition Name: A failed delete does not change any Flashcard
Test Case Summary: Reject a second delete after the Flashcard was already deleted
Test Preconditions: A stale Flashcard context is open after the target row has been deleted.
Steps: 1. Open the target Flashcard context in two Learner A sessions. 2. Delete the card successfully in Session 1. 3. Without reloading Session 2, attempt Delete Flashcard. 4. Reload the Deck.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Session 2 shows unavailable or Not Found, and no second success message appears. 2. [DB] No additional row is deleted or updated. All other Flashcards remain unchanged.

Test Scenario Name: Check and submit AI vocabulary input
Test scenarios' Precondition overall: Learner A is signed in with an Active account. The AI generation page and Groq service are available.
Test Condition Name: Valid AI input formats and limits are accepted
Test Case Summary: Require a supported Target language before generation
Test Preconditions: AI generation form is open with no Target language selected.
Steps: 1. Open Create Flashcards with AI. 2. Enter the vocabulary data without selecting Japanese or Chinese. 3. Attempt to select Generate preview. 4. Select each supported language option in turn and observe availability.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Generate preview is disabled while Target language is missing; only Japanese and Chinese are offered and the missing input is identifiable.

Test Case Summary: Parse line, comma, and mixed AI input
Test Preconditions: AI provider is available.
Steps: 1. For each separate pairwise test case in TD-DOC-AI-001, select the referenced Target language. 2. Enter the vocabulary list in the referenced separator format. 3. Select Generate preview. 4. Compare preview/failed-item counts with the parsed unique-item count, then Cancel before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Every non-empty line/comma item is parsed once; preview and failed notices account for the unique submitted items and the selected language.

Test Case Summary: Trim AI items and ignore blank entries
Test Preconditions: AI generation form is open.
Steps: 1. Select the Target language referenced by TD-DOC-AI-001. 2. Enter the test leading/trailing-space and blank-entry data. 3. Compare the unique-item counter with the expected non-blank trimmed items. 4. Generate preview and inspect item counts, then cancel.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Leading/trailing spaces are removed, blank entries are ignored, and only non-blank trimmed items reach preview processing.

Test Case Summary: Remove duplicate AI input before generation
Test Preconditions: AI generation form is open.
Steps: 1. Select the Target language referenced by TD-DOC-AI-001. 2. Enter the case/space/Unicode duplicate data. 3. Compare the unique-item counter with the test distinct-item count. 4. Generate preview and inspect item/notice counts, then cancel.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Inputs that are the same after normalization count as one unique item. The unique-item counter, preview count, and failed-item count include each normalized input only once. A separate duplicate notice is not required.

Test Case Summary: Accept exactly 50 unique AI vocabulary items
Test Preconditions: Groq is available and can process the maximum allowed input.
Steps: 1. Select the supported Target language in TD-DOC-AI-002. 2. Enter exactly 50 unique vocabulary items while remaining within 3000 characters. 3. Verify the item counter and select Generate preview. 4. Cancel after the result.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The 50-item input remains submit-enabled and enters preview processing without an item-limit error.

Test Case Summary: Accept an AI input of exactly 3000 characters
Test Preconditions: Groq is available and can process the maximum allowed input.
Steps: 1. Select the supported Target language in TD-DOC-AI-002. 2. Enter the exactly-3000-character vocabulary data while remaining within 50 unique items. 3. Verify the character counter and select Generate preview. 4. Cancel after the result.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The 3000-character input remains submit-enabled and enters preview processing without a character-limit error.

Test Condition Name: Empty, unsupported, or over-limit AI input is rejected
Test Case Summary: Reject 51 unique AI vocabulary items
Test Preconditions: AI generation form is open.
Steps: 1. Select a supported Target language. 2. Enter the 51-unique-item data in TD-DOC-AI-002 while remaining within 3000 characters. 3. Observe the counter and attempt Generate preview.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Generation is blocked with a clear maximum-50-items response and no preview is produced.

Test Case Summary: Reject an AI input of 3001 characters
Test Preconditions: AI generation form is open.
Steps: 1. Select a supported Target language. 2. Enter the 3001-character data in TD-DOC-AI-002 while remaining within 50 unique items. 3. Observe the counter and attempt Generate preview.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Generation is blocked with a clear maximum-3000-characters response and no preview is produced.

Test Case Summary: Reject a blank AI vocabulary list
Test Preconditions: AI generation page is available.
Steps: 1. Select a supported Target language. 2. Enter the all-blank/whitespace data from TD-DOC-AI-003. 3. Attempt Generate preview.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The input is rejected as empty after trimming and no preview is displayed.

Test Case Summary: Reject input when all AI items are unsupported or in the wrong language
Test Preconditions: AI generation page is available.
Steps: 1. Select the supported Target language referenced by TD-DOC-AI-003. 2. Enter the all-unsupported/wrong-language data. 3. Select Generate preview and inspect the result or failed-item notice.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] No preview card is available to save. Each rejected input is listed with a clear reason.

Test Case Summary: Generate valid items and report mismatched items
Test Preconditions: AI generation page is available.
Steps: 1. Select the Target language referenced by TD-DOC-AI-003. 2. Enter the mixed valid and mismatched vocabulary data. 3. Generate preview. 4. Compare valid-preview and failed-item counts with the test data, then cancel.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Valid selected-language items proceed to preview while mismatched/unsupported items are listed with reasons; counts account for every unique submitted item.

Test scenarios' Precondition overall: Learner A submitted a valid unique list with Japanese or Chinese selected. Groq is available.
Test Condition Name: A valid AI preview uses the required fields and language rules
Test Case Summary: Check Japanese preview fields for each script type
Test Preconditions: Japanese is selected and the vocabulary data covers all script test cases.
Steps: 1. Select Japanese and submit each Japanese script test case in TD-DOC-AI-004. 2. Inspect Term, Meaning, and Example sentence in Review Flashcards. 3. Verify the fields are editable. 4. Cancel between separate runs.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Accepted Kanji and Kanji-plus-Kana items contain a valid Title Case Sino-Vietnamese line in Term; Hiragana-only/Katakana items do not invent that line; Meaning and example follow Japanese-to-Vietnamese order.

Test Case Summary: Check Chinese preview field order
Test Preconditions: Chinese and Japanese generation runs can be performed for equivalent Han-character inputs.
Steps: 1. Generate each Chinese mapping test case in TD-DOC-AI-004. 2. Inspect Term, Meaning, and Example sentence placement. 3. Verify the fields remain editable. 4. Cancel between separate runs.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Chinese Term contains original vocabulary only; Meaning orders Title Case Sino-Vietnamese, optional Pinyin, then Vietnamese meaning; valid items remain editable.

Test Case Summary: Keep the same Sino-Vietnamese reading across Chinese and Japanese previews
Test Preconditions: Chinese and Japanese generation runs can be performed for equivalent Han-character inputs.
Steps: 1. Generate the Chinese test case for the test Han-character vocabulary in TD-DOC-AI-004 and record its Sino-Vietnamese interpretation. 2. Cancel. 3. Generate the corresponding Japanese test case. 4. Compare the interpretations while accounting for their different field placement.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Target-language selection changes approved field placement but does not turn the Sino-Vietnamese interpretation into a Vietnamese translation or an unrelated reading.

Test Case Summary: Show a valid example followed by its Vietnamese translation
Test Preconditions: The AI service returns complete preview content that can be reviewed.
Steps: 1. Generate each valid Target-language example test case in TD-DOC-AI-004. 2. Inspect Example sentence for a contextual target-language sentence followed by a non-empty Vietnamese translation. 3. Verify the item remains editable and available to save. 4. Cancel.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Every valid item shows a target-language example followed by a non-empty Vietnamese translation. The item can still be edited and saved.

Test Case Summary: Do not allow a generated item with an invalid example
Test Preconditions: The AI result contains an item whose example is missing the target-language sentence, missing the Vietnamese translation, or uses the wrong target language.
Steps: 1. Generate each invalid-example test case in TD-DOC-AI-005 one at a time. 2. Inspect the preview and failed-item notice. 3. Attempt to select the invalid item. 4. Cancel before the next test case.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The invalid item is not shown as a card that can be saved. Its original input is listed with a clear failure reason.

Test Case Summary: Handle a Japanese-script input with no confirmed meaning
Test Preconditions: The AI generation page is available and Japanese can be selected.
Steps: 1. Open Create Flashcards with AI. 2. Select Japanese. 3. Enter 日語本剝. 4. Select Generate preview. 5. Check the preview cards, failed items, and whether the item can be saved.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] BLOCKED: The requirement does not define whether this Japanese-script string must be rejected or shown for review. Do not mark Pass or Fail until PO/BA defines the expected behavior.

Test Condition Name: Partial or failed AI generation is clearly shown and not saved
Test Case Summary: Show valid partial results and reasons for failed items
Test Preconditions: The AI result contains both valid and failed items.
Steps: 1. Submit the partial-result data in TD-DOC-AI-005. 2. Check generated cards, selected count, and the failed-items message. 3. Try to select a failed item. 4. Cancel.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Valid items can be edited and selected. Each failed input shows a clear reason and cannot be selected or saved.

Test Case Summary: Keep line breaks and the correct preview layout
Test Preconditions: Preview contains multiline Term and Meaning content.
Steps: 1. Generate the multiline preview in TD-DOC-AI-006. 2. At desktop width, check that Term and Meaning start at the same level and have the same size, and that Example sentence uses the full row. 3. Edit all three fields and add line breaks. 4. Repeat at the supported mobile width.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Term and Meaning have the same width and height and keep line breaks. Example sentence uses the full row. No text overlaps or is cut off at supported desktop and mobile widths.

Test Case Summary: Handle an AI timeout without saving data
Test Preconditions: Test environment can induce or observe provider timeout/failure.
Steps: 1. Select a supported Target language and enter the valid timeout test data from TD-DOC-AI-007. 2. Generate preview under the timeout condition. 3. Wait only for the configured request deadline. 4. Inspect recovery controls and retry when the provider is restored.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] A readable timeout response appears at the configured deadline; no successful preview is shown for timed-out items and retry remains possible.

Test Case Summary: Handle an AI service failure without saving data
Test Preconditions: Test environment can induce or observe provider timeout/failure.
Steps: 1. Select a supported Target language and enter the valid failure test data from TD-DOC-AI-007. 2. Generate preview while the provider is unavailable or returns a processing failure. 3. Inspect the failure response and recovery controls. 4. Retry after service restoration.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] A readable generation-failed response appears; no failed item is presented as a successful preview and retry remains possible.

Test scenarios' Precondition overall: At least one valid preview card is available. Learner A owns the target Folder or Deck.
Test Condition Name: Selected valid preview cards are saved with the initial learning state
Test Case Summary: Save edited selected preview cards to an existing Deck
Test Preconditions: Valid selected preview cards are ready. Learner A owns a destination Deck with no duplicate normalized Terms. TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values are recorded.
Steps: 1. Record the TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting state. 2. In the TD-DOC-AI-008 preview, edit the referenced Term, Meaning, and Example sentence values and keep the intended cards selected. 3. Choose Existing Deck and select the owned destination state in TD-DOC-DECK-001. 4. Select Save Flashcards. 5. Reload the destination Deck and compare Dashboard/notification state with the starting state.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The success message shows the saved count, the destination Deck opens, and the edited values are displayed. Dashboard and notification values do not change. 2. [DB] One Flashcard row is created for each selected item with the correct user_id and deck_id, the three content fields, review_level=0, next_review=NULL, and last_recall_rating=NULL. notifications, study_session_records, and profiles.last_learning_activity_at do not change.

Test Case Summary: Create a new Deck and save selected cards together
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns a Folder without a normalized duplicate Deck name.
Steps: 1. In preview, select New Deck. 2. Choose the owned Folder and enter the referenced new Deck name data. 3. Select Save Flashcards. 4. Reload the Folder and created Deck.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] A success toast appears; exactly one new Deck is shown under the Folder and contains all selected valid cards. 2. [DB] Exactly +1 'decks' row and the expected 'flashcards' rows are inserted with consistent owner/folder/deck keys and initial SRS values; no partial Deck/card state or notification/activity change exists.

Test Case Summary: Save only selected valid items from a partial preview
Test Preconditions: Preview includes valid items and a failed-items notice.
Steps: 1. Select only the intended valid items. 2. Confirm failed items have no selectable card. 3. Choose an owned destination and save. 4. Reload the Deck.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Only the selected valid items appear in the Deck. Unselected and failed items are absent, and the success count is correct. 2. [DB] The created rows match only the selected valid items. No row is created for an unselected or failed item.

Test Case Summary: Save a card when optional Hiragana or Pinyin is missing
Test Preconditions: A valid selected Japanese or Chinese preview card has no optional reading. Learner A owns the destination Deck.
Steps: 1. Prepare the valid preview card without optional Hiragana or Pinyin. 2. Keep the card selected. 3. Choose the owned Existing Deck from TD-DOC-DECK-001. 4. Select Save Flashcards and reload the Deck.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The card saves successfully. Missing optional Hiragana or Pinyin does not cause a validation error. 2. [DB] One row is created with the entered content, correct owner and Deck, and initial SRS values.

Test Condition Name: Cancelled or invalid preview content is not saved
Test Case Summary: Cancel and discard an unsaved AI preview
Test Preconditions: An equivalent unsaved preview can be created for this discard action.
Steps: 1. Generate the unsaved preview in TD-DOC-AI-008 and record TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values. 2. Select Cancel. 3. Return to AI generation and the intended destination Deck. 4. Check Library, LEARN, DASH, shared view, and export sources.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The cancelled preview cannot be resumed and appears in no destination/related view. 2. [DB] No preview Flashcard/Deck rows are saved and TD-DOC-XMOD-001 values remain unchanged.

Test Case Summary: Refresh and discard an unsaved AI preview
Test Preconditions: An equivalent unsaved preview can be created for this discard action.
Steps: 1. Generate the unsaved preview in TD-DOC-AI-008 and record TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values. 2. Refresh the browser before saving. 3. Return to AI generation and the intended destination Deck. 4. Check Library and related views.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The refreshed unsaved preview cannot be resumed and appears in no destination/related view. 2. [DB] No preview Flashcard/Deck rows are saved and TD-DOC-XMOD-001 values remain unchanged.

Test Case Summary: Log out and discard an unsaved AI preview
Test Preconditions: An unsaved preview exists in a signed-in Learner A session.
Steps: 1. Generate an unsaved preview and record TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values. 2. Log out before saving. 3. Authenticate again and revisit AI generation and the intended destination Deck. 4. Check Library and related views.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Logging in again does not restore the unsaved preview or expose it in a destination/related view. 2. [DB] No preview Flashcard/Deck rows are saved and TD-DOC-XMOD-001 values remain unchanged.

Test Case Summary: Expire the session and discard an unsaved AI preview
Test Preconditions: An unsaved preview exists in a Learner A session that can be expired.
Steps: 1. Generate an unsaved preview and record TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting values. 2. Expire the session before saving. 3. Attempt save, then authenticate again and revisit the intended destination. 4. Check Library and related views.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Save requires authentication and the expired preview is not restored or exposed in a destination/related view. 2. [DB] No preview Flashcard/Deck rows are saved and TD-DOC-XMOD-001 values remain unchanged.

Test Case Summary: Block save when a selected card has a blank required field
Test Preconditions: Preview contains editable valid cards.
Steps: 1. Open the editable preview in TD-DOC-AI-009. 2. Remove one required field from a selected card while keeping a valid destination. 3. Attempt Save Flashcards. 4. Restore the field and repeat for the other required fields.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each selected card with a blank required field shows a validation message. Save does not succeed or leave the page. 2. [DB] No Flashcard or Deck row is created or updated. The destination remains unchanged.

Test Case Summary: Block save when no preview card is selected
Test Preconditions: Preview contains editable valid cards.
Steps: 1. Open the preview in TD-DOC-AI-009. 2. Deselect every valid card. 3. Choose a valid destination. 4. Attempt Save Flashcards.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Save is disabled or shows Select at least one Flashcard. No success navigation occurs. 2. [DB] No Flashcard or Deck row is created or updated. The destination remains unchanged.

Test Condition Name: Duplicate Terms in the selected existing Deck block only conflicting cards
Test Case Summary: Mark duplicate preview Terms for the selected existing Deck
Test Preconditions: Preview includes conflicting and non-conflicting items; at least two owned Decks have different Terms.
Steps: 1. Select Existing Deck and the first target in TD-DOC-DECK-001. 2. Select the conflicting and non-conflicting preview items from TD-DOC-AI-008/009. 3. Inspect duplicate markers and Save availability.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each selected Term that conflicts with the chosen Deck is clearly marked and blocks Save. Non-conflicting items remain available for review. 2. [DB] The duplicate check does not change data, and no conflicting row is created.

Test Case Summary: Update duplicate warnings after card or target changes
Test Preconditions: Preview includes conflicting and non-conflicting items; at least two owned Decks have different Terms.
Steps: 1. Start with the duplicate state in TD-DOC-AI-008/009 and TD-DOC-DECK-001. 2. One at a time, edit the conflicting Term, change the destination Deck, deselect and reselect the conflict, and remove the item. 3. Check the warning and Save state after each change. 4. Save only the final non-conflicting selection.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Duplicate state updates after every listed transition; resolving/deselecting/removing a conflict makes remaining valid items saveable. 2. [DB] No conflicting row is inserted and only the final non-conflicting selection is saved.

Test Case Summary: Handle a duplicate added by another session before save
Test Preconditions: Two browser sessions can access the same Existing Deck; preview initially has no conflict.
Steps: 1. In session one, select the Existing Deck and wait for a clean duplicate check. 2. In session two, create the conflicting card. 3. In session one, select Save Flashcards. 4. Observe refreshed preview, edit/deselect the conflict, and retry valid items.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Save does not create a duplicate. The Deck data is refreshed, the new conflict is clearly marked, and the user can edit or deselect it before retrying the valid items. 2. [DB] Only one row exists for the normalized Term. No partial duplicate row exists, and valid non-conflicting rows remain consistent.

Test Condition Name: A missing or invalid save target does not change data
Test Case Summary: Reject save if the selected existing Deck is deleted
Test Preconditions: Preview exists and an owned Existing Deck is selected in Session 1; Session 2 can delete that Deck.
Steps: 1. In Session 1, select the owned Existing Deck for the valid preview. 2. In Session 2, delete that Deck. 3. Without refreshing Session 1, select Save Flashcards. 4. Inspect target-recovery guidance and reload Library.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Save shows Not Found and asks the user to choose another Deck. No success message appears, and the deleted Deck remains absent. 2. [DB] No Flashcard or Deck row is created or restored, and no orphan row exists.

Test Case Summary: Reject save if the selected parent Folder is deleted
Test Preconditions: Preview exists and an owned Folder is selected for New Deck in Session 1; Session 2 can delete that Folder.
Steps: 1. In Session 1, select New Deck, choose the owned Folder, and enter a valid non-duplicate Deck name. 2. In Session 2, delete the selected Folder. 3. Without refreshing Session 1, select Save Flashcards. 4. Inspect recovery guidance and reload Library.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Save shows Not Found and asks the user to choose another Folder. No success message appears, and the deleted Folder remains absent. 2. [DB] No Folder, Deck, or Flashcard row is created or restored, and no orphan row exists.

Test Case Summary: Reject a duplicate new Deck name
Test Preconditions: Preview contains valid selected cards; the owned Folder already contains a Deck with the conflicting normalized name.
Steps: 1. In preview, select New Deck and the owned Folder. 2. Enter the duplicate Deck-name test case in TD-DOC-AI-009. 3. Select Save Flashcards. 4. Reload the Folder.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Save is blocked with a duplicate Deck-name message. No success message or second Deck appears. 2. [DB] No new Deck or Flashcard row is created, and the existing Deck remains unchanged.

Test Scenario Name: Enable public sharing for an owned Deck
Test scenarios' Precondition overall: Learner A is signed in with an Active account and owns the test Decks.
Test Condition Name: Enabling sharing creates one active public URL
Test Case Summary: Enable sharing and get an active public URL
Test Preconditions: The owned Deck has no active share row. TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting profile activity, notification, and study values are recorded.
Steps: 1. Record the TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting state. 2. Set TD-DOC-SHARE-001 to the unshared state and open its owned Deck from TD-DOC-DECK-001. 3. Select Share and inspect the Share Deck dialog and Public link. 4. Copy and open the link in an incognito window. 5. Compare Dashboard/notification state with the starting state.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Share Deck shows a read-only URL in /share/deck/{token} format. Copy link works, and the link opens a view-only page in incognito. Dashboard and notification values do not change. 2. [DB] Exactly one active deck_shares row is created with the correct deck_id and user_id, a unique 64-character lowercase hexadecimal share_token, is_active=true, and deactivated_at=NULL. Flashcard, SRS, and TD-DOC-XMOD-001 values do not change.

Test Case Summary: Reuse the same public URL while sharing is active
Test Preconditions: Owned Deck already has one active shared URL.
Steps: 1. Open the Deck and Share dialog. 2. Close it. 3. Select Share again. 4. Compare the Public link with the saved URL.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The existing Public link is shown unchanged. No second link or unexpected error appears. 2. [DB] No new deck_shares row is created. The same row remains the only active share for the Deck, and no unrelated row changes.
Execution Notes: Perspective: Positive/Repeat Action | Technique: State Transition

Test Condition Name: A missing Deck or another Learner's Deck cannot be shared
Test Case Summary: Reject sharing if the Deck is deleted first
Test Preconditions: Two Learner A sessions can access an owned unshared Deck; Session 2 has a stale Deck context.
Steps: 1. Open the same unshared Deck in two Learner A sessions. 2. Delete the Deck in Session 1. 3. Without reloading Session 2, attempt Share if the control remains available. 4. Reload both sessions.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Session 2 shows Deck unavailable or Not Found and no Public link is created. 2. [DB] No deck_shares row is created or updated, and the deleted Deck is not restored.

Test Scenario Name: View a shared Deck as a Public User
Test scenarios' Precondition overall: An incognito Public User session is available. Active and inactive share links are ready.
Test Condition Name: An active shared view shows approved read-only data
Test Case Summary: Show only approved data in the public view
Test Preconditions: Owned shared Deck contains known multilingual Flashcards and has an active URL.
Steps: 1. Open the active link in incognito without signing in. 2. Inspect the page text, cards, links, and controls. 3. Reload and use browser search to look for test private metadata labels.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The public page shows only the Deck name and each card's Term, Meaning, and Example sentence. Owner data, Folder data, IDs, SRS data, Dashboard data, and tokens are not shown.
Execution Notes: Perspective: Security/Positive | Technique: Approved Fields Check

Test Case Summary: Keep line breaks in the public view
Test Preconditions: Active shared Deck includes multiline and markup-like content test data.
Steps: 1. Open the active TD-DOC-SHARE-002 link in incognito. 2. Compare the test line breaks in Term, Meaning, and Example sentence with the saved data. 3. Reload and compare again.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] All stored line breaks remain visible in the corresponding public card fields after reload, without clipping or overlap.

Test Case Summary: Show markup-like content as plain text
Test Preconditions: Active shared Deck includes multiline and markup-like content test data.
Steps: 1. Open the active TD-DOC-SHARE-002 link containing markup-like content in incognito. 2. Inspect all public fields. 3. Interact with and reload the page while observing navigation, controls, and browser execution.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Markup-like content is plain text; no script, injected control, redirect, or page corruption occurs.

Test Case Summary: Block restricted actions in the public shared view
Test Preconditions: A Public User can open an active shared Deck URL; restricted action routes are known where applicable.
Steps: 1. Open the active shared URL as Public User. 2. Verify edit, delete, import/copy, and learning controls are absent. 3. Attempt each known restricted route/action directly where the UI does not expose it. 4. Reload the owner and public views.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Restricted controls are absent and direct attempts return Permission Denied/authentication-required feedback without exposing private content.

Test Condition Name: An empty, invalid, or inactive shared link shows no private data
Test Case Summary: Show the empty state for an active shared Deck
Test Preconditions: Empty Deck has an active share URL.
Steps: 1. Open the link in incognito. 2. Observe the content region and reload.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] A no-Flashcards empty state is shown without an error and no edit action is exposed.

Test Case Summary: Show unavailable for an invalid public link
Test Preconditions: Invalid-token, disabled-token, and deleted-Deck-link test cases exist.
Steps: 1. Open the invalid-token test case in TD-DOC-SHARE-003 in a fresh incognito tab. 2. Refresh the page and inspect displayed content.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The page displays This shared Deck is unavailable and reveals no Deck/Flashcard content.

Test Case Summary: Show unavailable for a disabled public link
Test Preconditions: Invalid-token, disabled-token, and deleted-Deck-link test cases exist.
Steps: 1. Open the inactive-token test case in TD-DOC-SHARE-003 in a fresh incognito tab. 2. Refresh the page and inspect displayed content.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The page displays This shared Deck is unavailable and reveals no Deck/Flashcard content.

Test Case Summary: Show the old link as unavailable after the owner deletes the Deck
Test Preconditions: Invalid-token, disabled-token, and deleted-Deck-link test cases exist.
Steps: 1. Save the active public URL in TD-DOC-SHARE-003. 2. Delete the associated Deck as its owner. 3. Open the previous URL in a fresh incognito tab and refresh.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The previous URL displays This shared Deck is unavailable and reveals no deleted content.

Test scenarios' Precondition overall: Learner A owns Decks with active and inactive share links. An incognito session is available.
Test Condition Name: Disabling sharing blocks the old link after refresh
Test Case Summary: Disable sharing and block the old page after refresh
Test Preconditions: The owned Deck has an active URL already open in incognito. TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting profile activity, notification, and study values are recorded.
Steps: 1. Record the TD-DOC-XMOD-001 starting state. 2. In the owner session, use the active/open-page state in TD-DOC-SHARE-001 and select Disable link. 3. Confirm owner feedback. 4. Refresh the already-open incognito page and open the old URL in a new incognito tab. 5. Compare Dashboard/notification state with the starting state.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The owner sees that the Public link is disabled. After refresh, both the already-open page and a new request to the old URL show unavailable and no Deck content. Dashboard and notification values do not change. 2. [DB] The active deck_shares row changes to is_active=false and has a deactivated_at value. Flashcard, SRS, and TD-DOC-XMOD-001 values do not change.

Test Case Summary: Keep sharing disabled when it is already inactive
Test Preconditions: Owned Deck has no active share row.
Steps: 1. Open the owned Deck. 2. Inspect Share state and attempt the available disable flow if presented. 3. Reload the Deck.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Sharing remains disabled and no new Public link or token appears. 2. [DB] No deck_shares row is created. All inactive rows remain inactive, and no unrelated row changes.
Execution Notes: Perspective: Positive/Repeat Action | Technique: State Transition

Test Condition Name: Re-enabling sharing creates a new link
Test Case Summary: Create a new link after re-enable and keep the old link blocked
Test Preconditions: Owned Deck has a saved token that was disabled.
Steps: 1. Select Share on the disabled Deck to re-enable. 2. Compare the new Public link with the saved old link. 3. Open both links in separate incognito tabs and refresh.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] New link differs and opens the view-only Deck; old link remains unavailable after refresh. 2. [DB] A new active 'deck_shares' row with a distinct unique token is inserted; old row remains inactive with deactivation timestamp and at most one active row exists for the Deck.

Test Scenario Name: Export an owned Deck to Excel
Test scenarios' Precondition overall: Learner A is signed in with an Active account. An Excel-compatible app and export test data are available.
Test Condition Name: A successful export has the correct data and filename
Test Case Summary: Export cards currently in the Deck with the correct columns and row order
Test Preconditions: The owned Deck contains a known set of current Flashcards.
Steps: 1. Open the owned Deck and select Export. 2. Open the workbook. 3. Compare its row count, row order, numbering, headers, and cell values with the current Deck.
Expected Result: 1. [UI/File] One valid .xlsx file downloads with the headers No, Term, Meaning, and Example Sentence. Numbering starts at 1, every current card appears once, and the row order matches the Deck.

Test Case Summary: Create the export filename with the UTC+7 date
Test Preconditions: Owned export Deck contains filename-normalization test data; execution can cover the test UTC+7 date boundary.
Steps: 1. For each filename and UTC+7 boundary test case in TD-DOC-EXPORT-001, export the owned Deck. 2. Inspect the downloaded filename. 3. Compare normalized Deck-name and date components with the test boundary.
Expected Result: 1. [UI/File] Filename is deck_<normalizedDeckName>_<YYYYMMDD>.xlsx; Deck name is lowercase with spaces converted to hyphens and unsafe characters removed/replaced, and date uses UTC+7.

Test Case Summary: Keep line breaks and special characters in the workbook
Test Preconditions: Owned export Deck contains multiline and supported special-character content.
Steps: 1. Export the TD-DOC-EXPORT-001 Deck containing multiline and supported special content. 2. Open the workbook. 3. Compare each exported content cell with the saved data.
Expected Result: 1. [UI/File] Supported line breaks and special characters remain intact in the corresponding workbook cells without truncation or corruption.

Test Case Summary: Exclude private and system data from the workbook
Test Preconditions: Private and system values for the owned export Deck are recorded.
Steps: 1. Export the TD-DOC-EXPORT-001 Deck. 2. Open the workbook. 3. Search visible/hidden sheets, columns, named ranges, and document properties for the test private/internal values.
Expected Result: 1. [UI/File] Workbook contains only No, Term, Meaning, and Example Sentence; owner data, IDs, SRS fields, share token, Dashboard metrics, hidden private columns, and extra private sheets are absent.
Execution Notes: Perspective: Security | Technique: Approved Fields Check

Test Condition Name: A failed export creates no file and changes no data
Test Case Summary: Block export for an empty owned Deck
Test Preconditions: Learner A owns an empty Deck.
Steps: 1. Open the empty state of TD-DOC-DECK-001. 2. Inspect or attempt Export. 3. Check the browser download list.
Expected Result: 1. [UI/File] Export is disabled or the system displays This Deck has no Flashcards to export; no workbook or partial file appears.

Test Case Summary: Reject export if the Deck is deleted first
Test Preconditions: Two Learner A sessions can access the same non-empty owned Deck; Session 2 has a stale Deck page.
Steps: 1. Open the same non-empty Deck in two Learner A sessions. 2. Delete the Deck in Session 1. 3. Without reloading Session 2, attempt Export. 4. Check downloads and reload Library.
Expected Result: 1. [UI/File] Session 2 receives Deck unavailable/Not Found feedback and no workbook/partial file appears.

Test Case Summary: Block export from the public shared view
Test Preconditions: An active public shared URL exists and a Public User/incognito session is available.
Steps: 1. Open the active shared URL in incognito. 2. Verify no Export control or download link is displayed. 3. Attempt the known export route directly as Public User if available. 4. Confirm no download starts.
Expected Result: 1. [UI/File] Public view exposes no Export control/file and a direct attempt returns Permission Denied/authentication-required feedback without private content.

Test Case Summary: Handle export failure and retry without partial files
Test Preconditions: Environment can induce one internal export failure for an owned non-empty Deck, then restore service.
Steps: 1. Open the owned Deck under the induced failure condition. 2. Select Export. 3. Inspect user feedback and browser downloads. 4. Restore service and immediately select Export again. 5. Open the resulting workbook.
Expected Result: 1. [UI/File] First attempt shows a user-friendly generic failure and creates no partial/corrupt file; immediate retry succeeds with one valid workbook.

Test Scenario Name: Protect private DOC pages and actions
Test scenarios' Precondition overall: Sessions are available for a logged-out user, a Deactivated Learner, a non-owner Learner, an Admin, and a Public User.
Test Condition Name: Logged-out or expired sessions cannot open protected DOC pages
Test Case Summary: Block protected DOC pages after logout or session expiry
Test Preconditions: A valid Learner session is logged out or expired; protected Deck and AI URLs are known.
Steps: 1. For each unauthenticated or expired-session route test case in TD-DOC-RBAC-001, open the protected route. 2. Use browser Back and refresh. 3. Attempt any visible protected action.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] The user is sent to Login or sees an authentication-required message. Protected content and actions cannot be used through Back or refresh.

Test Condition Name: Unauthorized actors cannot change DOC data
Test Case Summary: Block DOC changes by unauthorized actors
Test Preconditions: The RBAC actor/action data and owner-controlled target data are ready. The owner's visible data is recorded.
Steps: 1. Record the owner's visible Deck, Flashcard, and share data. 2. Using each non-owner, Deactivated Learner, Admin, and Public User session in TD-DOC-RBAC-001, try the listed create, edit, delete, AI save, sharing, and export actions. 3. Reload the owner's pages and public view after each actor.
Expected Result: 1. [UI] Each unauthorized action is hidden or returns Permission Denied or Account Restricted. No success message or private content is shown. After reload, the owner's Deck, Flashcard, and share data remain unchanged.
